note: Original places, batch 4 of 4: smelters, mints, shrines, towers, markets, workshops and the places where strange materials fall. Each is a Location under a wild or city. Written for Asetheria; no third-party text.

entries.name: The Copper Smelts
entries.summary: A smoky quarter by the two harbours where ore from the islands is turned into the metals that arm and ornament the League.
entries.body:
A grimy quarter beside the western harbour, crowded with furnaces, casting-pits and the sheds of founders who have worked the same alloys for six generations. Ore comes in by ship from the islands, and bars of bronze and brass go out the same way. The air tastes of metal and the water of the harbour has a green sheen.

## What is worked here

The smelts turn out [[Copper]] and [[Tin]], cast the two into [[Bronze]], and mix copper with calamine for the yellow [[Brass]] that temple doors and trumpets are made of.

## Visiting

The founders' guild runs a hall and a hostel for visiting buyers. The furnaces are not for strangers, and the guild's apprentices wear scars for it.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: an alloy recipe is missing from the guild's strongbox. The founder who kept it died last month, and his apprentices are blaming each other.

entries.name: The Imperial Mint
entries.summary: A fortified workshop beside the temple of warning where the empire's coin is struck and every ounce of precious metal is weighed twice.
entries.body:
A fortified workshop attached to the temple of the goddess of warning, from which the Imperium's coin takes its name. Bullion comes in under escort, assayers test every bar, and the dies are struck by hand in rooms with no windows. Every worker is searched at the door and searched again at the exit.

## What is worked here

The mint strikes the coinage from [[Gold]], [[Silver]] and the pale gold-silver alloy [[Electrum]], which the old kings of the east used and the mint still keeps for ceremonial issues.

## Visiting

The mint is closed to the public. The temple's front hall displays a specimen coin of each issue, and the guards watch the visitors, not the coins.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the weights have been shaved by a fraction. The difference, spread over ten years, is a fortune, and the quaestor knows.

entries.name: The Iron Furnaces
entries.summary: A ring of blast-houses inside the fortress-city's outer wall, where the families who armed the legions still forge their steel.
entries.body:
A ring of squat blast-houses inside the outer wall of the citadel, working day and night in shifts. The families who control them have been armourers since before the empires and have no wish to be anything else. Their steel is sold to anyone who can pay, and refused to anyone who can pay too little.

## What is worked here

The furnaces smelt [[Iron]], temper it into [[Steel]] by a method the families do not discuss, and forge a few small ingots a year of [[Cold Iron]], used against things that will not be struck with anything else.

## Visiting

A buyer is received in the front hall. The families' own armourers wear their best work, and a visitor who admires a blade is offered a price.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a family has begun making blades that do not ring. A weaponsmith from a rival house has bought one and shown it to a priest.

entries.name: The Silver Drifts
entries.summary: Mine tunnels and washing-floors in the hills behind the naval city, where slaves and free miners dig lead and silver for the fleet.
entries.body:
A network of tunnels and washing-floors in the hills behind the naval city, worked by gangs of slaves and the free miners who supervise them. The ore is lead with a thin vein of silver, and the washing-floors run white with the washed stone. The fleet is paid for by the silver, and the miners are paid in less.

## What is worked here

The drifts produce [[Lead]], used for pipes and sling-bullets, and refined [[Silver]] that the city turns into its famous owl-stamped coinage.

## Visiting

The washing-floors are open to the public in the dry season. The tunnels are not, and the overseers do not like anyone to count the miners.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the miners are planning an uprising. A free-born foreman has offered to open the gates for a share.

entries.name: The Treasury of Hours
entries.summary: A columned vault beneath the royal palace where the King of Kings keeps the metals he will not spend and the strange ones nobody can name.
entries.body:
A vast vault beneath the royal palace, its pillars carved with the hours of the day and its doors opened only at the hour the king chooses. It holds the empire's tribute in bullion, the king's private hoard of strange metals, and a room that the keepers do not enter after dark.

## What is stored here

The vault holds ingots of [[Orichalcum]], the pale, ancient, golden alloy; rare white [[Platinum]], which no smith in the empire knows how to melt; and a single plate of [[Adamantium]] that the court believes to be older than the dynasty.

## Visiting

The vault is closed to everyone except the king and his treasurer. A visitor to the palace may see the great door and nothing else.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the forbidden room has been opened. The treasurer has resigned, and no one will say why.

entries.name: The Fallen-Star Shrine
entries.summary: A small, windswept sanctuary on the mountain's warm flank where a black stone fell from the sky and the priests have kept it ever since.
entries.body:
A small sanctuary on the mountain's warm flank, built around a pit in which a black, pitted stone lies half-buried, where it fell. The priests keep a lamp burning beside it and sweep the ground every morning, and the pilgrims come on foot and are not allowed to touch it.

## What is kept here

The shrine holds [[Star Metal]], the iron that falls from the sky, and a few splinters of the blue-white [[Celestium]] that, the priests say, fell with it and has been glowing ever since.

## Visiting

The shrine is open to pilgrims at dawn. Offerings are accepted and not discussed.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the stone is warmer each year. A priest has begun recording the temperature and has told no one the figures.

entries.name: The Cold Forge
entries.summary: A black, windowless smithy beneath the black ridge where the metals that drink light are worked by smiths who do not speak.
entries.body:
A windowless smithy beneath the black ridge, so cold that the water in the quenching trough is permanently skinned with ice. The smiths do not speak, do not wear gloves and do not say who they work for. Their products are dark, matte and heavy, and an armourer who has seen one will not describe it.

## What is worked here

The forge works the light-drinking [[Darksteel]], the shadow-ore [[Tenebrium]], the ember-veined [[Infernal Iron]] and the cold, northern [[Ironfell]], all of which arrive by night in wagons without markings.

## Visiting

The forge has no door that a visitor has found. The caravans that pass at night say that the glow from the vents is black.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the smiths are making a single item, and have been for sixty years. They are nearly done.

entries.name: The Assayers' Tower
entries.summary: A neutral laboratory-tower in the treaty city where rare and magical materials are tested, certified and priced for the courts of three empires.
entries.body:
A neutral tower in the treaty city, built by a pact of the three powers to settle disputes about what is worth what. Its assayers test every rare and magical material that crosses a border, and a stamp from the tower is accepted at every court. The tower has no allegiance, which is why it is still standing.

## What is tested here

The assayers handle [[Mithril]], [[Arcanaite]], [[Nullstone]], [[Tethtrium]], [[Embersteel]], [[Shattergleam Crystal]] and [[Anchoring Gems]], and keep a sample cabinet of each that scholars may consult by appointment.

## Visiting

A petitioner may bring a sample for a fee. The tower's door-wardens are impartial, and politely armed.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a sample certified last week has proved fake. The assayer who stamped it is missing, and the tower wants the case quietly closed.

entries.name: The Scar Fields
entries.summary: A stretch of black, glassy desert where the divine war left its mark, and strange stones that burn, scream or sink are picked up by the desperate.
entries.body:
A broad stretch of fused black ground in the divine-tainted part of the desert, ridged and glassy and warm even at night. The scavengers who work here go in masked and in pairs, and what they bring out is sold in a back room in the nearest oasis, with the prices set by the buyer's nerves.

## What is found here

The fields yield black [[Acher Obsidian]], ember-hot [[Hellstone]], dull [[Daemon Iron]], the burning [[Inferno Crystal]], the cold, dripping [[Styxium]], the pitted [[Titanium (Carceri)]] and the shrill [[Shrieking Steel]] that sings when struck.

## Visiting

A guide is essential and a priest is advised. The oasis rest-house keeps a ledger of those who went in.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the fields have grown by a mile in a year. A scavenger says the ground is breathing out.

entries.name: The Thin Places
entries.summary: Three bare terraces high on the mountain where the world is worn so thin that the high powers' metals can be gathered by a patient climber.
entries.body:
Three bare terraces near the peak, so high that the air is thin and so quiet that a man can hear his own blood. Visitors report that the light is wrong: too clear, too sharp, as if a veil had been lifted. The sky-priests say this is where the world is worn thin enough for gifts to pass through.

## What is found here

The terraces give [[Hallowed Steel]], the shining [[Valhallium]], the weightless [[Aerialite]], the white [[Ivorite]], the harmonic [[Idyllium]], the cold [[Prismatic Ice]], the shifting [[Prismetal]] and the heavy, patient [[Aximium]].

## Visiting

The climb takes three days and a vow of silence. Those who come down speak of a light they cannot describe.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: someone has been climbing the terraces to take, not to gather. The metals are less bright each month, and something is aware.

entries.name: The Living Stones
entries.summary: A deep forest clearing where green-veined rocks grow like fungus, clay breathes and geodes open at dawn like eyes.
entries.body:
A circular clearing deep in the forest where the stones are warm, the soil is soft and nothing grows taller than a man's knee. The rocks are veined with green and seem to gain a few inches each year. A forest tribe keeps the clearing and speaks of it as a sleeping thing.

## What is found here

The clearing yields [[Chlorophyte]], the growing green ore, the soft [[Clay of Life]], the opening [[Gaia Geode]] and the beating red [[Heart Stones]] that the tribe will not sell for any price.

## Visiting

A visitor is received by the tribe at the edge. They are polite, patient and unmoved by money.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the clearing has begun to spread, and the tribe is moving its camp. They have asked an outsider to help them find out why.

entries.name: The Drowned Workshop
entries.summary: A ruined stone workshop half-sunk in the lake, still turning slowly, where the lost craft of an older people lies in the silt.
entries.body:
A ruined workshop half-sunk in the shallows of the great lake, its stone walls green with weed and its great wheel still turning slowly in the current. The lake-fishers avoid it, and the few divers who have gone in report rooms of machinery, lit by a pale light that does not come from the surface.

## What is found here

The silt around the workshop yields the clicking [[Mechanite]], the amorphous [[Meld]], the lightless [[Voidmetal]], the pale [[Cosmilite]] and the dripping, weightless [[Etherplasm]].

## Visiting

A fisher's hut on the nearest shore rents boats and tells stories. The stories agree on the wheel and disagree on everything else.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the wheel turned faster this week. Something in the workshop has been wound.

entries.name: The Spice Wharf
entries.summary: A fragrant quay where ships from the farthest east unload cassia, pepper and ginger, and the whole harbour smells like a feast.
entries.body:
A long stone quay on the naval city's eastern harbour, lined with warehouses that are sealed at night with three locks. Ships from the farthest east unload sacks that smell of cinnamon and fire, and the wharf's factors weigh each in front of the buyer and in front of the tax-clerk.

## What is sold here

The wharf trades [[Trade Cassia]], [[Black Pepper]] and the knobbed [[Root of Warmth]], all of which are priced by the pinch, and all of which are adulterated by the time they reach a village market.

## Visiting

The wharf is open to every buyer. A pickpocket's guild runs a tidy business in the crowd.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a ship has docked that carries no spice. The harbour-master has logged it as pepper, and a crate has already been unloaded.

entries.name: The Amber Stalls
entries.summary: A narrow lane of jewellers' booths in the capital where northern amber is polished, set and sold with a story attached.
entries.body:
A narrow lane near the great circus, lined with the booths of the jewellers who work northern amber. Every piece comes with a story: a fly caught in sap, a drop that wept from a sister's tears, a stone that a legionary brought home from the cold north. The booth-keepers are the finest liars in the capital, and the finest eyes.

## What is sold here

The stalls sell worked [[Northern Amber]], black [[Jet]] set beside it for contrast, and polished lumps of [[Pumice]] for cleaning the stones.

## Visiting

The lane is open daily. A buyer is advised to carry a loupe and a friend.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a new stall sells amber with no flaws and no inclusions. It is glass, and a dozen senators' wives are wearing it.

entries.name: The Tyrian Vats
entries.summary: A reeking dye-works on the temple-port's far shore where snails and insects are crushed into the colours of kings.
entries.body:
A long row of vats on the far shore of the temple-port, downwind and downstream of everything, where the stench is the first thing a visitor notices and the last thing a resident does. Shell-heaps taller than the sheds stand on the beach, and the workers' hands are stained from the wrist down.

## What is made here

The vats turn [[Purple-Snail]] into the true purple reserved by law for rulers, and [[Scarlet-Grain]] into a red that rivals it. The two together make a robe that a village could not afford.

## Visiting

Buyers come by boat. The dyers are proud, secretive and permanently stained.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a vat of true purple has been stolen. The thief will be found by the colour of his hands.

entries.name: The Herbalists' Lodge
entries.summary: A quiet courtyard behind the oracle's temple where physicians and herb-wives trade cures, warnings and the day's gossip.
entries.body:
A quiet courtyard behind the oracle's temple, planted with pots and hung with drying bunches, where the physicians of the city and the herb-wives of the villages meet to trade. It is the only place in the city where the two groups talk as equals, and the lodge-keeper makes sure they do.

## What is traded here

The lodge stocks [[Temple Hyssop]], [[Madness-Cure Hellebore]] under lock and key, and the pungent [[Garlic]] and spiral-flowered [[Birthwort]] that the midwives swear by.

## Visiting

The lodge is open to anyone with a complaint. The lodge-keeper is a good listener and a better prescriber.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a new physician is selling cures that work too well. The lodge suspects he is poisoning the villagers to create the need.

entries.name: The Wise Owl Inn
entries.summary: A rambling inn beside the old city wall where a little yellow-eyed owl presides over the common room and the landlord's secrets.
entries.body:
A rambling, three-storey inn built against the city wall, its common room dark with generations of smoke. A little owl lives in the rafters, fed by the landlord and treated by the regulars as the establishment's conscience. Business here is done in whispers, and the owl is thought to listen.

## What is here

The inn's sign shows the [[Owl of the Wise Goddess]], and its cellar holds an excellent local wine.

## Visiting

The inn has twelve beds and three rules. The landlord recites them on arrival and the owl nods.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the landlord uses the owl as an excuse for knowing things he should not. He has been selling what he hears.

entries.name: The Beekeepers' Hall
entries.summary: A low stone lodge on the Oros slope where the hill villages weigh, grade and seal their honey, and the thyme smell reaches the road.
entries.body:
A low stone lodge on the Oros slope where the beekeepers of the hill villages bring their combs once a year for weighing, grading and sealing under the hall's stamp. The hall's cellar holds the village's reserve, and a jar sealed here carries a name that can be sold in the capital.

## What is sold here

The hall sells the dark honey of the [[Mountain Honeybee]], flavoured with [[Hymettan Thyme]], and the wax that goes with it.

## Visiting

The annual grading draws buyers from three cities. A beekeeper who cheats is expelled, and his bees are said to leave with him.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a village's honey has been graded higher than its quality. The grader has a new house, and a debt that vanished.

entries.name: The Lyre-Makers' Row
entries.summary: A street of luthiers by the stadium where tortoise shells become the sounding-boards of every music-school's instruments.
entries.body:
A street of luthiers near the games stadium, each with a window full of lyres in every state of completion. The best are made on shells chosen by the maker himself, and the shells are cured for a year before they are strung. A passing musician can tell a row-made lyre by the first note.

## What is made here

The luthiers use the shells of the [[Hill Tortoise]], bought from hill villages on the understanding that the animals are returned to the wild after a season.

## Visiting

A player can try an instrument. A buyer who is serious is offered a seat, a cup and a long lecture.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the tortoise supply is failing. The luthiers have begun buying from poachers, and a shell with a mark on it has turned up.

entries.name: The Dream Dormitory
entries.summary: A long, cool hall in the oracle's precinct where the sick sleep among harmless snakes and wake with a cure or a riddle.
entries.body:
A long, cool hall in the sanctuary precinct, lined with cots and patrolled by slow, olive-coloured snakes that no one has ever seen bite. The sick are admitted after a ritual bath and a night of fasting, and lie down to sleep. In the morning they report their dreams to a priest, who interprets them as a prescription.

## What lives here

The hall is the home of the [[Healer's Serpent]], bred in the temple for six hundred years and known to the priests by name.

## Visiting

The dormitory is open to the sick and their families. The priests accept donations and do not guarantee results.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: one pilgrim's dream gave a prescription that cured her. The priest who interpreted it has since vanished, and it was not a standard dream.

entries.name: The Stork Roof
entries.summary: The great flat roof of the sun-temple, where a dozen storks nest in the shadow of the gold dome and are forbidden to be harmed.
entries.body:
The wide, flat roof of the sun-temple, reached by a spiral stair and crowned with a gold dome. A dozen stork nests sit among the chimneys, each a mass of sticks the size of a cartwheel. The priests treat the birds as lodgers whose rent is luck, and the city's children watch them with spy-glasses from the neighbouring towers.

## What lives here

The roof is the summer home of the [[Roof-Stork]]. A priest records the date of the first arrival each year, and the record is consulted by the farmers.

## Visiting

The roof is open to anyone who climbs the stair. The storks are not impressed by anyone.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: no stork has returned this spring. The priest has hidden the fact and is leaving offerings.

entries.name: The Wreckers' Beacon
entries.summary: A lighthouse of black stone on the strait's southern cape whose keepers say they save ships, and whose neighbours say they sink them.
entries.body:
A tall, black lighthouse on the strait's southern cape, with a fire-basket that burns pitch and a keeper's house that has seen more weather than visitors. The keepers claim to guide ships through the rocks; the neighbouring villagers claim to have seen the light move on stormy nights, and the cove below is strewn with timbers.

## What lives here

The tower is a roost for the [[Never-Landing Swift]], which wheels around the lantern at dusk, and the keepers keep a tally of them as a weather-sign.

## Visiting

A sailor may ask for a bed in the keeper's house. The keeper asks what the ship carries, which is a reasonable question for a lighthouse.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the keepers are wreckers. Every wreck is blamed on the strait, and every cargo is sold in the next valley.

entries.name: The Stilted Archive
entries.summary: A library on wooden stilts in the middle of the marsh, where the scribes who cut the reeds also copy the books that need to be forgotten.
entries.body:
A library on wooden stilts in the middle of the marsh, reached by a plank causeway that the keepers pull up at night. The scribes who live here cut their own reeds, mix their own ink and copy the texts that the great libraries would rather not keep. Dampness is the archive's enemy, and the smell is its signature.

## What is made here

The archive's copyists use the finest [[Pen-Reed]] from the surrounding fen, and sell sealed copies to scholars who ask no questions.

## Visiting

A visitor must be vouched for by a scribe. The causeway is narrow, and the keepers like it that way.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a book is missing, one that the keepers forbade themselves to copy. Its absence has attracted three separate buyers.

entries.name: The Caravan Stone
entries.summary: A walled rest-house at a desert crossroads where every caravan master has carved a name, and the cook's cumin is famous on three continents.
entries.body:
A walled rest-house at a desert crossroads, named for the single huge stone in its courtyard on which every caravan master has carved his name for a thousand years. The cook's stew is the only reason many travellers choose this route, and the stone is the only reason the cook has not been poached.

## What is served here

The kitchen cooks with [[Caravan Cumin]] and the red [[Red-Hand Leaf]] the cook's family has grown for generations, and finishes with a sprinkle of [[Sweet-Root]].

## Visiting

The house charges by the bed and by the meal. A traveller who carves a name on the stone is expected to buy a round.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a name on the stone has been scratched out, and the cook says she did not do it. The name was a satrap's.
